mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized suggests inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% does not lead to a statistically significant negative 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increase does not lead to a statistically significant positive 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced output and profitability.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decline does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% does not lead to a statistically significant negative 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests strong labor market conditions, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not lead to a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates increased consumer spending, which is a positive signal for economic growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increase does not lead to a statistically significant positive 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity increases.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 2% does not lead to a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).
